draft.title: Galaxies, stars and black holes
card: Galaxy
A galaxy is a huge group of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity. The universe holds billions of galaxies.
Star
A star is a ball of hot gas that gives off its own light. Each galaxy has billions of stars. Our Sun is one star in the Milky Way galaxy.
Black hole
A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape from it.
Light-year
A light-year is the distance light travels in one year. It is a unit of distance, not of time, and it is used for the huge gaps in space.
draft.remember: Stars make up galaxies, and a light-year measures distance. Not even light escapes a black hole.

a.q: A star is 8 light-years from Earth. What does the 8 light-years tell us?
opts: The distance light travels in 8 years
The time the star takes to orbit Earth
The number of years the star has existed
The time the star takes to burn out
a.why: A light-year is a distance, so 8 light-years is how far light travels in 8 years. It is easy to read it as a time, but the unit measures how far away something is.
a.clue: Is a light-year a time or a distance?

b.q: Why can astronomers not see light coming from inside a black hole?
opts: Its gravity is too strong for light to escape
It is too far away for light to reach Earth
It is made of gas that does not give off light
Its light is too faint to be seen by telescopes
b.why: Gravity in a black hole is so strong that not even light escapes, so no light leaves it. Distance and faintness are tempting, but they would not explain why light from nearby stars still reaches us.
b.clue: Think about what gravity does to light there.

a.best: The distance light travels in 8 years

b.best: Its gravity is too strong for light to escape

problems.detail: "Each galaxy has billions of stars" is not true of every galaxy. Dwarf galaxies can hold only millions of stars or fewer. "Large galaxies have billions of stars" or "many galaxies" would be accurate.
The clue "Think about what gravity does to light there" gives the answer away, because only one option mentions gravity.
The clue "Is a light-year a time or a distance?" practically gives the answer, because only one option describes a distance.

The why's reasoning is muddled. It says distance and faintness "would not explain why light from nearby stars still reaches us", which does not clearly show why those options are wrong. It should say that no light escapes a black hole whatever its distance or brightness.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, but both clues give the answer away, and the card wrongly says every galaxy has billions of stars. The why for question b also uses confusing reasoning.

Light-year

proposal.remember: Stars make up galaxies, and a light-year measures distance. Not even light escapes a black hole.

a.q: A star is 8 light-years from Earth. What does the 8 light-years tell us?
opts: How far light travels in 8 years
How far the star moves in 8 years
How many years the star has been shining
How many years the star takes to orbit Earth
a.why: A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, so 8 light-years is how far light travels in 8 years. It is not about how far the star moves, and it is not a time, even though the unit has year in its name.
a.clue: Whose journey is the unit based on?

b.q: Why can astronomers not see light coming from inside a black hole?
opts: Its gravity is too strong for light to escape
It is too far away for light to reach Earth
It is made of gas that does not give off light
Its light is too faint to be seen by telescopes
b.why: Gravity in a black hole is so strong that no light escapes, whatever its distance or brightness. Distance is tempting, but light reaches us from galaxies much further away than many black holes.
b.clue: Light from far more distant objects still reaches Earth.

a.best: How far light travels in 8 years

b.best: Its gravity is too strong for light to escape
